name: CineOpcode
meaning: Opcode word at +0 of a cinematic script record, dispatched by Cine_RunOpcodes 0x5621b0. A record is an 8-BYTE HEADER {u16 opcode; u16 count; u32 payloadPtr} followed by count * g_cineOpStride[opcode] bytes, where the stride table at 0x5816fc reads [0,8,8,4,2,2,4,2,2] - so opcodes 1..8 have strides 8,8,4,2,2,4,2,2. Cine_RecordSize 0x561800 computes the step exactly. Cine_AdvanceScriptCursor adds 2 more for opcodes 4/5/7/8 when the COUNT IS ODD: those four all have stride 2, so an odd count leaves the stream 2-byte misaligned and the extra 2 is ALIGNMENT PADDING. record+2 is the count, not a flags word. Handler addresses and opcode semantics are verified. 0x563470, called by Cine_RunOpcodes, initialises every non-empty record's cursor to its LAST key using (count-1)*stride, so dispatch does not necessarily begin at k=0.

name: CINE_OP_ATTACH_A
meaning: -> 0x563060: finds the attach entry (cine+0x8e8, stride 0x1c) whose PARENT (+4) is the target and, by keyframe parity, calls 0x562660 (attach child to parent joint with offset/rot) or 0x5626b0 (detach). Inert in this build: attachCount 0x958 is cleared and never made positive (entry layout verified at 0x562660).

name: CINE_OP_ATTACH_B
meaning: same handler as 7 with the parity bit inverted - its attach/detach partner. Inert for the same reason.

name: CINE_OP_KEY_POSITION
meaning: position keyframe -> Cine_OpKeyPosition 0x562e00; applies through the object's SetPosition vtable slot (+0x1c), with an optional world offset from cine+0x8c0.

name: CINE_OP_KEY_ROTATION
meaning: rotation keyframe -> Cine_OpKeyRotation 0x562ee0; writes ScnObject.rot at obj+0x14 directly, using shortest-path angle interpolation.

name: CINE_OP_PLAY_ANIM
meaning: play an animation on the target: Cine_OpStartAnim 0x562f70 then Cine_OpAdvanceAnim 0x562fa0 (the latter skipped when the object's flags bit 0x20 is set).

name: CINE_OP_FLICKER_PHASE_A
meaning: NOT a plain hide (verified from 0x562fc0-0x562fef). Computes b = parity of ((dword at record+4) - recordAddress) >> 1, which for cursor = record+8+2k is the parity of the keyframe index k. b != 0 CLEARS ScnObject flags 0x800 (visible), b == 0 SETS it (hidden). So this opcode makes the object alternate: hidden on even k, visible on odd k.

name: CINE_OP_FLICKER_PHASE_B
meaning: the same handler with b INVERTED, so the opposite phase: visible on even k, hidden on odd k. Opcodes 4 and 5 are two phases of an alternating visibility effect, not a set/clear pair.

name: CINE_OP_KEY_CAMSCALAR
meaning: scalar keyframe -> Cine_OpKeyCamScalar 0x562ff0, applied only on the selector-0 (camera) path, into Cine.camScalar +0x8d8.
